title: The Story Doesn’t End at the Keyboard: WPMTest × Glossika
description: Meet WPMTest’s language-learning affiliate partner: how Glossika teaches, ten courses from our revival series, free-course details, and a practical study routine.
intro: A language deserves more than a moving history and a beautifully placed accent mark. It deserves to be heard. Answered. Used in a conversation that wanders gloriously off-script.

Our Language Revival series began with the people who kept their languages alive through pressure, punishment, and generations of hard work. Now we’re excited to give readers another way to move from reading those stories to building a practice of their own: WPMTest has teamed up with Glossika as an affiliate partner.

The connection makes sense. WPMTest gives your fingers a place to get familiar with written forms. Glossika brings sentence-based listening and speaking training into the picture. Your keyboard has had plenty to say. Your voice deserves a turn.

sections.heading: Meet Glossika: give the words a voice
paragraphs: Glossika is a language-training platform built around sentences. Its published method uses complete utterances, native-speaker audio, and repeated practice, so you encounter vocabulary inside something you can actually say. You hear how words connect, where the rhythm falls, and how familiar structures change when the meaning changes.

Glossika describes its review system as spaced repetition: studied material returns over time, with the schedule shaped by your practice. The aim is to make useful patterns more accessible when you need them. Repetition can look modest on a calendar; remembering the sentence when you want to use it is the part that matters.

Its web/Legacy guides describe full-practice exercises including listening, dictation, typing, recording, and recall, plus a listening-only mode. Features depend on the version and plan. The newer mobile app also offers native-speaker content and structured training; its interface and subscriptions differ from Legacy.

sections.heading: Why this belongs beside our revival series
paragraphs: After researching these histories, “That’s interesting” felt like an unfinished ending. We wanted a next step: somewhere a curious reader could hear Welsh, return to Manx, or deliberately choose Hailu rather than accidentally studying another Hakka variety.

Glossika’s published web catalog includes nine free courses that overlap with this collection. That gives readers a concrete way to explore languages beyond the familiar handful on a typical app menu. Irish is offered too, under different access terms. Hawaiian remains part of our series, but it is not listed in the Glossika catalog we checked.

Revitalization still belongs to speakers, families, teachers, and communities. An app can make practice easier to reach; it cannot restore language rights, replace an immersion school, or grant cultural belonging. We’re enthusiastic about this extra doorway because it leads toward more use, while the people carrying the language remain the centre of the story.

sections.heading: A fifteen-minute routine worth coming back to
paragraphs: Here is our suggested way to combine the tools. It is a flexible practice plan, not a tested promise of fluency. Start small enough that tomorrow’s session still sounds inviting.

steps.title: Two minutes: know what you are saying
steps.text: Choose one language and one variety. Read a short explanation from a teacher or a speaker-led resource. Learn what your practice sentence means before chasing pronunciation or speed. If the spelling system is unfamiliar, begin with its basic sounds and marks.

steps.title: Eight minutes: listen, answer, repeat
steps.text: Work through your due Glossika reviews, then add a manageable amount of new material. Listen once for meaning, again for rhythm, and try speaking before checking the answer. When available in your plan, record a short attempt and compare it with the model. Let difficult items stay difficult for a while; that is useful information.

steps.title: Three minutes: make the keyboard familiar
steps.text: Return to the matching WPMTest drill for accents, letters, or input-method practice. If you use your own passage, choose text whose language and use rights you can verify. Do not copy a paid course library into another tool. Accuracy and correct written forms matter more here than a heroic WPM screenshot.

steps.title: Two minutes: take one thing into your day
steps.text: Say a sentence without looking, write a personal note, or plan a question for your next lesson. Later, look for a class, conversation group, broadcast, or book made by speakers. The aim is a reason to use the language after the timer stops.

sections.heading: Who is likely to enjoy it?
paragraphs: This approach is appealing if you like hearing real sentences, speaking aloud, and returning to a compact daily routine. It can give a learner who recognises words on a page a structured reason to practise producing them. The best fit depends on your starting point and the material you choose.

Glossika’s own grammar guidance says it is not a substitute for an introductory grammar course and recommends having the basics first. If you are completely new, pair it with a teacher, beginner resource, or pronunciation introduction. Understanding why a sentence works makes repeated practice more useful than repeating a mystery very confidently.

Use your first sessions to judge the fit: can you follow the meaning, hear a useful model, and explain what you practised? For progress, revisit a small set of sentences a week later and note what you can understand or say without a prompt. A longer streak and faster copying are satisfying, but they answer different questions.

sections.heading: Free courses, trials, and the version you choose
paragraphs: Glossika’s published web/Legacy pricing and free-course guide list the nine courses in our table as free to study with an account. Certain premium features require a subscription. Irish is available but is not on that nine-course list. A free course and a time-limited trial are different offers.

The website currently advertises a seven-day full-access trial without a credit card. Check the offer on your destination page before signing up. We have not added an exclusive discount or a coupon: none was supplied with our affiliate link.

There is also a newer iOS/Android app. Glossika’s migration guidance distinguishes its subscriptions from Legacy, including whether an existing subscription transfers. Do not assume a web purchase unlocks the newer app or that its free-access rules are identical. Compare the exact app, course, billing period, renewal terms, and cancellation route before paying.

sections.heading: What teaming up means—and why we’re excited
paragraphs: WPMTest is participating as a Glossika affiliate. If you follow our referral link and make a qualifying purchase, we may receive a commission. You can use WPMTest without buying anything, and our link takes you to Glossika’s website, where you select your language.

This is a referral relationship. It does not mean Glossika wrote or endorsed our historical articles, verified our typing passages, or guarantees anyone’s learning outcome. Our course notes are based on the published information linked below, rather than a claim that we personally completed every course.

What excites us is the possibility of turning curiosity into a repeatable habit. Read a language’s story. Hear it spoken. Try a sentence. Come back tomorrow. A little more room for Welsh, Gàidhlig, Tâi-gí, or Manx in an ordinary day is a worthwhile next step. We’re delighted to help you find it.
